title: A little less work, every time
subtitle: Sliding Window
body: Imagine a frame that holds exactly three readings. Slide it one place to the right: two readings stay inside, one leaves, and one enters. The previous sum already contains almost everything you need. Remove the outgoing reading and add the incoming one. The frame represents a contiguous interval; it cannot skip an inconvenient reading. Try changing one value before looking at the code, then predict which windows it will affect.
invariant: The running sum is exactly the sum of the current window. A fixed-size window is a different problem from a variable-length window whose validity depends on a condition.
pitfall: Updating the best answer before a full window exists gives the wrong result. Initialize the best sum below every valid sum so negative inputs work.
code: for (int right = 0; right < a.length; right++) { sum += a[right];

checkpoint.question: Which statement captures the key idea?
options: Add the incoming value and subtract the outgoing one

takeaways: The running sum is exactly the sum of the current window. A fixed-size window is a different problem from a variable-length window whose validity depends on a condition.
Updating the best answer before a full window exists gives the wrong result. Initialize the best sum below every valid sum so negative inputs work.

blocks.title: Reuse the work you already did
blocks.text: For 2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2 with k = 3, the first full window sums to 8. Moving right removes 2 and adds 1, so the next sum is 7. The following windows sum to 9 and 6. The answer is 9. The largest element alone is not the answer: the problem asks for three consecutive readings.

blocks.title: The frame and the sum agree
blocks.text: After processing index right, the running sum contains exactly the readings from max(0, right-k+1) through right. Only compare with best once the frame contains k readings. Initializing best to zero breaks all-negative inputs. Keep best unset, or at the smallest representable value, until the first full window exists.

blocks.title: What the constraint tells you
blocks.text: Recomputing each of n-k+1 sums takes O(nk). Reusing the sum takes O(n) time and O(1) extra space. This fixed-size technique works with negative readings. A variable-size window that shrinks whenever a sum is too large needs additional assumptions; negative values can break that shrinking rule.
